targets.authors: Amick BC, Hogg-Johnson S, Latour-Villamil D, et al
targets.title: Protecting construction worker health and safety in Ontario, Canada: identifying a Union safety effect
targets.evidence_quote: This study updates Amick et al,20 using data from 2012 to 2018, with the same objective of estimating the association between business unionisation and the risk of various types of workers’ compensation injury claims.
targets.outcome_quote: Company unionisation was associated with a lower risk of lost-time workers’ compensation injury claims, corroborating a similar study from an earlier time period. The protective effect of unionisation declined as company size decreased. In contrast to the previous study, a positive relationship between company unionisation and no-lost-time claim incidence was not found, due in part to a methodological refinement.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Lost-time and severe-injury findings replicated; authors explicitly contrast failure to repeat the no-lost-time finding. Confirmation of the lost-time effect is a component comparison, not an overall verdict overriding this contrast.

reasoning: New 2012–2018 administrative sample retests Amick et al. (2015), the explicitly named prior study. Other unionisation studies are background. Original-data sensitivity estimate is incidental to this new-sample replication.
